 Regarding delays in tax refunds, the Minister of Finance stated, "Whoever is at fault will bear the consequences."
 VTV.vn - If taxpayers provide complete documentation but the tax authorities fail to process it within the deadline, they must be held accountable, including providing material compensation.
 Đài truyền hình Việt Nam • 12/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Equality between the tax authorities and taxpayers. 
 On the morning of November 12th, during a National Assembly questioning session, Representative Tran Anh Tuan ( Ho Chi Minh City) pointed out the current situation where businesses are fined 0.03% per day for late tax payments. The 2019 Tax Administration Law stipulated that the State must pay interest of 0.03% per day to businesses for late payments. However, the 2025 Tax Administration Law no longer includes this provision.
 The delegate asked the Minister to clarify the principle regarding whether the State pays interest at the same rate as the enterprise if it is late in making payments.
 Responding to the delegates' questions regarding the responsibility of state agencies, especially tax authorities, for delays in tax refunds, Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan emphasized the need to ensure the principle of equality: "Whoever is at fault bears the responsibility." 
 On the morning of November 12th, Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan answered questions before the National Assembly. 
 According to the Minister, currently, individuals and businesses who are late in paying taxes are subject to administrative penalties and late payment fees. Therefore, if taxpayers have provided complete and correct documents but the tax authorities, specifically the receiving officers, fail to process them within the deadline, then they must be held accountable, including providing material compensation. Minister Ngo Van Tuan emphasized that the fundamental issue is that the documents must be correct, complete, and in accordance with the law .
 The Minister stated that the tax authorities are currently striving to shorten the tax refund process. For the green channel (refund first, audit later), the refund time is only 7 days. For cases requiring audit before refund, the tax authorities are also coordinating closely to handle them.
 However, according to the Minister, although 100% of taxpayers' records have been submitted online, the process of verifying and cross-checking invoices still takes time and poses potential risks for some groups of businesses. The Ministry of Finance will continue to study this issue in detail in the future.
 Reiterating the principle of "whoever is at fault bears the responsibility," Minister Ngo Van Tuan emphasized that if the fault lies with the State or tax officials, then those officials must bear responsibility according to the principle of equality before the law.
 It's normal for businesses to withdraw from the market. 
 Meanwhile, delegate Nguyen Duy Thanh (from Ca Mau province) questioned the Minister of Finance about the sharp increase in the number of dissolved businesses. He also asked whether the government intends to extend the value-added tax reduction policy into 2027, given that the policy is set to expire on December 31, 2026.
 Regarding this issue, Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan stated that in the first nine months of this year, approximately 172,000 businesses withdrew from the market, while 222,000 businesses re-entered and participated in the market.
 According to the Ministry of Finance's analysis, among the businesses withdrawing from the market, 50% have temporarily suspended operations, 30% have completed dissolution procedures, and 20% are in the process of ceasing operations.
 You may also like Conversely, thanks to efforts to improve the investment and business environment, reduce tax obligations, and shorten the time and cost of administrative procedures, the number of businesses entering the market has reached over 222,000. Notably, registered capital increased by 38% compared to the same period.
 Analyzing the group of businesses that have temporarily ceased operations or dissolved, Minister Ngo Van Tuan stated that approximately 90% operate in the trade and service sectors; about 89% of businesses did not generate revenue in 2026, meaning they had already ceased operations before then. In addition, about 70% of these businesses had already stopped operating before 2026. 
 On the morning of November 12th, the National Assembly conducted a question-and-answer session on issues related to the financial sector.
 Explaining the large number of businesses withdrawing from the market, the Minister said that this is normal. In business operations, some businesses succeed while others fail.
 In particular, in a transparent business environment that facilitates the operation of individuals and businesses, the procedures for entering the market are relatively simple. However, the procedures for exiting the market involve fulfilling financial obligations. Besides obligations to the state budget, taxes, and social insurance, businesses must also fulfill obligations to suppliers and lending banks.
 The Minister stated that the Ministry of Finance has directed the implementation of tax code cleaning. "For businesses that have 'cleaned' their financial obligations, the procedure for exiting the market will only take one day," the Minister emphasized.
 Regarding the further reduction of value-added tax (VAT) by 2%, from 10% to 8%, the Minister stated that the Prime Minister is directing the Ministry of Finance to carefully study and evaluate this issue, along with the legal framework for investment and business activities in the remaining months of 2026 and the beginning of 2027.
 In particular, it is necessary to closely monitor market developments, especially the petroleum and raw materials markets, in order to have timely and appropriate solutions. At the same time, the ultimate goal of maintaining growth above 10% and controlling inflation at around 4.5% must still be ensured.
 2.5 million tax identification numbers remain uncleaned. 
 During the questioning session, delegate Hoang Ngoc Dinh (Tuyen Quang delegation) cited data from the Tax Department showing that there are currently over 2.5 million tax identification numbers that need to be reviewed, standardized, and cleaned up. This includes businesses that have not been operating at their registered addresses for decades.
 "What is the responsibility of the Ministry and the tax authorities for this backlog? And what are the solutions for handling it in the future?", questioned representative Hoang Ngoc Dinh.
 Responding to the issue raised by the delegates, Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan affirmed that cleaning up tax identification numbers for businesses that are no longer operating at their registered address or have ceased operations is a mandatory requirement. 
 Minister of Finance Ngo Van Tuan affirmed that cleaning up tax identification numbers is a mandatory requirement.
 You may also like According to the Minister, one of the reasons Vietnam was placed on the list of non-cooperating countries in the tax system by the Global Forum and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) is because it has not yet completed the data cleaning process for tax identification numbers.
 Since the beginning of the year, the tax sector has cleaned up 777,000 tax codes. However, there are still about 2.5 million tax codes belonging to the status of businesses and household businesses that have ceased operations (03) or are no longer operating at the registered address (06).
 "This is a huge amount of work and needs to be addressed before the OECD review in the second quarter of 2028. The results will determine whether Vietnam is removed from the watchlist or continues to be classified as uncooperative on tax matters, which could impact the investment environment and economic development," Minister Ngo Van Tuan emphasized.
 To accomplish this task, the Ministry of Finance has reported to the Government. Last night (November 11th), the Ministry of Finance also submitted an official report to the Standing Committee of the National Assembly, proposing that the procedures for cleaning up tax identification numbers be included in the National Assembly's work program at this session.
 Notably, this includes the waiver of financial obligations for businesses and household businesses that have ceased operations for the past five years or more, particularly business license tax. The Minister stated that while business license tax has been abolished since January 1, 2026, significant outstanding payments remain. In addition, there are penalties for late payments.
 After processing and clearing these financial obligations, the tax authorities will proceed to close the tax identification numbers, thereby cleaning up the business environment, creating a safe environment, and preventing the exploitation of inactive tax identification numbers for tax evasion and illegal business activities in the future.
